summary.text: A previously healthy 12-year-old female presented after a 4-day history of flu-like symptoms, malaise and low-grade fever with progressively worsening left iliac fossa pain that interfered with ambulation and sleep, followed by vomiting and hospital admission. She appeared acutely ill, had no rash, and had left iliac fossa tenderness with focal guarding and a positive psoas sign.

Laboratory tests were normal apart from leukocytosis. Pelvic ultrasound showed a well-defined left adnexal heterogeneous echogenic mass with internal cystic areas, and an ovarian tumor was suspected. Pelvic MRI showed a left adnexal mass, the tumor markers were negative, and isolated tubal torsion was suspected, so surgery was scheduled.

The next day itchy fluid-filled blisters appeared over the face, abdomen and back, so surgery was postponed two days; the rash increased while the left iliac fossa pain and fever resolved. Chickenpox was diagnosed from the characteristic rash. The patient did not receive antibiotics, other medical therapy or surgery.

The mass slightly increased in volume on repeated ultrasound despite clinical improvement, and the patient was discharged and followed with serial pelvic ultrasonography. Ten days after discharge the mass showed cystic changes and had markedly decreased, and at six weeks it measured 3 cc, with spontaneous radiologic resolution of the abscess reported.

ambiguities.issue: The case-presentation segments describe a left adnexal mass lesion (suspected ovarian tumor, then isolated tubal torsion) and never use the word abscess; the tubo-ovarian abscess diagnosis is stated in the abstract and discussion without a stated diagnostic basis. No aspiration, culture or organism is reported.

ambiguities.issue: The mass volumes conflict: the case text says the repeated ultrasound showed an increase from 27 cc to 40 cc and cites Figure 3A, while the Figure 3A caption gives 16 cc after 2 weeks and the Figure 1 caption gives 40 cc for the ultrasound it shows (cited for the initial ultrasound).
